Internal probe and retirement paths belong to the core after exclusive creation, including their directory names in the managed parent. Mode 0700 excludes other OS users, but another process running as the same OS user can still replace those paths. Active same-user replacement of these internal paths is unsupported. Rename, unlink and directory removal there remain pathname operations, with no atomic inode-conditional deletion guarantee. Preexisting name collisions refuse before adoption or overwrite. Working Context edits and unrelated public backup names retain the documented preservation rules and final-sample limits. Private-namespace residuals were demonstrated by three synthetic same-user substitutions: an unknown retirement destination can be overwritten, a replacement predecessor can be deleted after its inode check, and a replacement retirement directory can be removed after its directory check. Those probes are retained as unsupported-operation evidence and are not passing preservation controls. They do not change the caller-owned public-name requirements. No provider or live trial ran for this clarification.
